CRES.G2.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.SELF_LIKES.mastery: States good things about himself or herself (my eyes, my voice, I can run, I help others) as made by God (Psalm 139:13: you knit me together in my mother's womb), and lists five chores done at home (sweeping, washing utensils, fetching water, making the bed, feeding animals). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: who is this person to you
CRES.G2.CREATI.MY_FAMILY.EXTENDED_FAMILY.mastery: Names family members (father, mother, brothers, sisters) and the extended family (grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins), says belonging to a family gives love and help, and that Cornelius and all his family worshipped God together (Acts 10:2). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

CRES.G2.CREATI.MY_FAMILY.SHARED_ITEMS.mastery: States items a family shares (food, utensils in turn after washing, chairs, the table, water, books, a radio or TV) to foster unity, and four items that should not be shared for health (toothbrush, towel, comb, underwear, handkerchief, razor blade), because they carry germs from one person to another. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

CRES.G2.CREATI.CREATION_OF_THE_SKY_SUN_..mastery: Says God made the lights in the sky on the fourth day (Genesis 1:14-19): the sun to rule the day, the moon to rule the night, and the stars; they mark days, seasons and years; God saw that it was good. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception. Practical, marked by the teacher with the KICD rubric (CRE.G2.RUBRIC.1.1, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.1.2, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.1.3, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.1.4, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.1.5, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.1.6), never as a phone question: b) draw the sun, moon, and stars to appreciate God’s creation.

Lists why Christians read the Bible: it is God's word, it guides how to live (Psalm 119:105: your word is a lamp for my feet, a light on my path), it teaches about God and Jesus, it comforts and helps us pray; and says families can read it together. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception. Practical, marked by the teacher with the KICD rubric (CRE.G2.RUBRIC.1.1, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.1.2, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.1.3, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.1.4, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.1.5, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.1.6), never as a phone question: e) list the number of times they read the Bible as a family; f) watch a video clip of children reading the Bible; g) in groups sing a song about the Bible, ‘My Bible and I, ooh..........’; h) read and recite Psalms 119:105.

CRES.G2.THE_HO.DIVISIONS_OF_THE_BIBLE.OL.mastery: States the Old Testament has 39 books, names Genesis and Exodus as its first two books, and knows the Bible has two divisions (Old and New Testament). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

CRES.G2.THE_HO.BIBLE_STORY_THE_CALL_OF_..mastery: Retells 1 Samuel 3:3-10: the boy Samuel was sleeping in the house of the Lord; the Lord called "Samuel!"; three times he ran to Eli thinking Eli called; Eli understood it was the Lord and told him to answer; the Lord called again and Samuel said "Speak, for your servant is listening." Lesson: listen to God and obey, and answer when called. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: why Daniel was thrown to the lions
CRES.G2.THE_HO.BIBLE_STORY_DANIEL_IN_TH..mastery: Retells Daniel 6: officials tricked King Darius into a law that no one should pray to anyone but the king for thirty days; Daniel still prayed three times a day at his open window towards Jerusalem; he was thrown into the den of lions; God sent his angel and shut the lions' mouths; in the morning Daniel was unharmed and the king praised God. Lessons: pray always, trust God, God protects, be faithful even when it is hard. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception. Practical, marked by the teacher with the KICD rubric (CRE.G2.RUBRIC.2.1, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.2.2, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.2.3, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.2.4, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.2.5, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.2.6), never as a phone question: c) apply lessons learnt in day-to-day life.

forms: what happened to the flour and oil
CRES.G2.THE_HO.THE_BIBLE_STORY_THE_WIDO..mastery: Retells 1 Kings 17:7-16: in a drought the brook dried up and God sent Elijah to Zarephath; a widow was gathering sticks to cook a last meal from a handful of flour and a little oil for herself and her son; Elijah asked her to make him a small loaf first, promising God would keep the flour and oil from running out; she obeyed, and the flour and oil did not run out until the rain came. Lessons: God provides, share even when we have little, trust and obey God's word. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

CRES.G2.THE_EA.THE_BIRTH_OF_JESUS_CHRIS..mastery: Relates Luke 2:15-20: after the angels left, the shepherds hurried to Bethlehem and found Mary, Joseph and the baby lying in a manger; they spread the word about the child; they returned glorifying and praising God for all they had heard and seen. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

Describes Luke 2:22-38: Mary and Joseph took baby Jesus to the temple in Jerusalem to present him to the Lord; they offered a pair of doves or two young pigeons; Simeon took Jesus in his arms and praised God; Anna the prophetess thanked God and spoke about the child. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: gift from a wise man or a shepherd
what to say to a stranger's gift
CRES.G2.THE_EA.KINDNESS_OF_THE_WISE_MEN..mastery: Lists the three gifts (gold, frankincense and myrrh, Matthew 2:11), says the wise men gave them out of love and worship, and knows the safety rule for children: politely refuse gifts from strangers and tell a trusted adult. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception. Practical, marked by the teacher with the KICD rubric (CRE.G2.RUBRIC.3.1, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.3.2, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.3.3, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.3.4, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.3.5, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.3.6), never as a phone question: b) demonstrate assertiveness by refusing gifts from strangers.

CRES.G2.THE_EA.JESUS_CALMS_THE_STORM.CAL.mastery: Narrates Matthew 8:23-27: Jesus and his disciples were in a boat; a furious storm came and waves swept over the boat; Jesus was sleeping; the disciples woke him, "Lord, save us! We're going to drown!"; he asked why they were afraid, rebuked the winds and waves, and it was completely calm; they were amazed. Lessons: trust Jesus in trouble, call on him, he has power over nature. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

CRES.G2.THE_EA.MIRACULOUS_CATCH_OF_FISH..mastery: Retells Luke 5:3-9: Jesus taught from Simon's boat; he told Simon to go into deep water and let down the nets; Simon said they had worked all night and caught nothing, but because Jesus said so he would; they caught so many fish the nets began to break and two boats were so full they began to sink; Simon fell at Jesus' knees. Lessons: obey Jesus, trust him, do not give up, Jesus provides. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

CRES.G2.THE_EA.HEALING_THE_MAN_WITH_A_W..mastery: Retells Matthew 12:9-13: in the synagogue on the Sabbath there was a man with a shrivelled hand; the Pharisees asked if it was lawful to heal on the Sabbath; Jesus said a person would lift a sheep out of a pit on the Sabbath, and it is lawful to do good; he told the man "Stretch out your hand" and it was completely restored. Lesson: show compassion and do good to others. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception. Practical, marked by the teacher with the KICD rubric (CRE.G2.RUBRIC.3.1, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.3.2, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.3.3, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.3.4, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.3.5, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.3.6), never as a phone question: b) mention occasions they prayed to God for healing.

forms: what happened on the third day
CRES.G2.THE_EA.EASTER.EASTER_LOVE.mastery: Says Jesus died on the cross on Good Friday as a sign of God's great love (John 3:16), was buried and was raised on the third day (1 Corinthians 15:3-4), and lists activities done in church at Easter: special services, prayers, singing, Bible reading, Palm Sunday processions, sharing with the needy. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception. Practical, marked by the teacher with the KICD rubric (CRE.G2.RUBRIC.4.1, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.4.2, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.4.3, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.4.4, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.4.5, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.4.6, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.4.7, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.4.8, CRE.G2.RUBRIC.4.9), never as a phone question: b) demonstrate kindness by sharing items with others.

Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception. CRES.G2.CHRIST.HONESTY.TELL_TRUTH.mastery: Gives reasons for telling the truth: God wants us to be truthful (Proverbs 12:17, 19: truthful lips endure forever), people trust us, lies lead to more lies and trouble, it keeps friendships; and recognises honest acts (owning up, returning lost items, not copying). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception. CRES.G2.CHRIST.THANKFULNESS.THANK_OTHERS.mastery: Lists why we thank others: it shows we appreciate them, makes them happy, encourages them to help again, builds friendship, and God tells us to give thanks in all circumstances (1 Thessalonians 5:18); and says when to thank (when given something, helped, served food, taught). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception. CRES.G2.CHRIST.FORGIVENESS.PRODIGAL_SON.mastery: Tells the story of Luke 15:11-24 in order for a drama: the younger son asked for his share, went to a distant country and wasted it; a famine came and he fed pigs; he came to his senses and went home to say sorry; his father ran to him, hugged him, gave him the best robe, a ring and sandals and held a feast. Lesson: God forgives, and we forgive others. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception. forms: name an item you carry to school
CRES.G2.CHRIST.RESPONSIBILITY.SCHOOL_ITE.mastery: Names items carried to school (books, pencils, rubber, ruler, crayons, school bag, water bottle, lunch box, sweater) and how a responsible child cares for them: cover books, keep them in the bag, label them, not lend carelessly, bring them back home; doing it well as for the Lord (Colossians 3:23). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception. forms: a way to help at home
CRES.G2.CHRIST.WORK.HELP_PARENTS.mastery: Mentions ways children help parents at home (sweeping, washing utensils, fetching water, feeding animals, caring for younger siblings, making the bed, picking litter) and says helping shows love and that work is good. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception. CRES.G2.THE_CH.PRAYER.FRIEND_MIDNIGHT.mastery: Retells Luke 11:5-10: a man went to a friend at midnight asking for three loaves because a traveller had arrived and he had nothing to give; the friend said the door was locked and his children were in bed; because the man kept asking, the friend got up and gave him what he needed; Jesus said "Ask and it will be given to you". Lesson: keep praying. Also knows the first lines of the Lord's Prayer (Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done). forms: a role of the Holy Spirit

Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
